item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Dodgers will look to clinch a series victory over the Cincinnati Reds in Ohio.
Most recently, they won by a score of 4-0 on Tuesday.
Bob Nightengale of USA Today wrote: “The Los Angeles Dodgers can clinch their 13th division title in 14 years with a victory over Cincinnati today or a loss later at night by the San Diego Padres
Los Angeles Dodgers Announced Andy Pages Update
The Dodgers continue to play without Andy Pages, as he has been out of action since August 21 with an injury.
MLB.com wrote (on September 15): “Has progressed to hitting baseballs, with the next step being hitting off the Trajekt machine.”
Before getting hurt, Pages had been batting .272 with 134 hits, 21 home runs, 80 RBIs, 72 runs and 12 stolen bases in 128 games.
Looking At Pages
Pages is in the middle of his third season at the MLB level (all with the Dodgers).
He has already helped the Dodgers win two World Series titles (2024-25).
The 25-year-old also made his first career MLB All-Star Game earlier this season.
Looking At The Dodgers Right Now
The Dodgers are in the middle of another outstanding season.
They are at the top of the National League West with a 92-59 record in 151 games.
Over their last ten games, the Dodgers have gone 8-2 (and they are 45-31 in 76 games on the road).
Following their series with the Reds, they will return home to host the San Francisco Giants on Friday night in California.
Looking At The Reds Right Now
The Reds come into the day as the last-place team in the National League Central with a 70-81 record in 151 games.
They have gone 3-7 over their last ten games (and are 36-40 in 76 games at home in Cincinnati).

item.content:encoded:
Edwin Diaz signed a three-year, $69 million contract in December. It made him baseball's highest-paid reliever by average annual salary. His first season for the Los Angeles Dodgers has not matched that price tag.
Diaz opened the year on a rocky note. He allowed one run through his first five outings. Two rough appearances followed.
Doctors then found loose bodies in his right elbow. He had arthroscopic surgery and missed roughly 100 days.
He returned in late July and posted mixed results. The Dodgers placed him back on the injured list Aug. 18. This time, doctors diagnosed inflammation on the right side of his neck.
Diaz has an 11.85 ERA in 16 appearances this season. He has thrown 13 2/3 innings for the Los Angeles Dodgers. The right-hander has struck out 19 batters and walked 10.
That uneven form has created real uncertainty about his spot on the postseason roster.
Edwin Diaz's Roster Spot Now in Doubt
insider Ken Rosenthal addressed Diaz's situation on the show "Foul Territory." He said the Dodgers will pick their 26 best players, regardless of salary.
The club has called this year's pitching staff its deepest ever heading into October.
Rosenthal added that if evaluators view Diaz as not good enough, the Dodgers will leave him off. Rosenthal called it a "win-at-all-costs kind of industry."
Manager Dave Roberts has not guaranteed Diaz a spot either. "We have to go with our best pitchers," Roberts said. Diaz has not pitched well enough yet during his rehab assignment.
He allowed five runs while recording two outs in his Sept. 13 outing. He is set for another rehab appearance Sept. 16, with an expected return in late September.
The stakes are real. The Dodgers clinched a playoff berth Monday with a win over the Cincinnati Reds.
Latest Updates on Edwin Diaz, Shohei Ohtani
The Dodgers updated their injury report this week. Several key players remain sidelined heading into the stretch run.
Diaz remains on the 15-day injured list with neck inflammation. He is on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day injured list with a left knee and right biceps injury, retroactive to Sept. 8. He could return as a hitter as soon as Sept. 23. He is not expected to pitch again until 2027. He began a swing progression Sept. 15, hitting off a tee.
Outfielder Andy Pages has a fractured left hand. He landed on the 10-day injured list Aug. 22. He has progressed to hitting baseballs off a machine, with an expected return in late September as well.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched a postseason spot for the 14th consecutive season and are closing in on a 13th National League West title during that span.
Also of importance for the Dodgers is finishing with a top two record in the NL as it would come with a first-round bye in the playoffs. That could be of particular value to a slew of injured Dodgers, including Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing and Edgardo Henriquez.
Dodgers updates
Dalton Rushing
Rushing made a surprising return on Sept. 1 from a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow, but only managed to appear in four games off the bench before going back on the 10-day injured list. That came after Rushing was scratched from the lineup due to right elbow trouble that stemmed from his attempt at a throwing progression.
The Dodgers have since ruled out Rushing possibly catching again this year, but they remain hopeful he will be an option as a left-handed bat off the bench.
“Dalton’s doing well,” manager Dave Roberts said on SportsNet LA. “Building up his progression.”
Shohei Ohtani
Ohtani started his swinging progression on Tuesday by hitting off a tee. Roberts said he “felt good” doing so and is going to continue moving along.
“I don’t know what’s in store for tomorrow, but I know there’s going to be a consistent buildup. Don’t know when the time to return to play is, but today was positive and hopefully we can just keep building toward that,” Roberts said.
Roberts added he believes Ohtani will return at some point in the regular season, but cautioned, “Whether it happens or not is to be determined.”
Ohtani is eligible to be activated off the 15-day injured list Sept. 23.
Andy Pages
Pages has been swinging a bat for several days and took a step forward on Tuesday by hitting off pitching machine. Next for Pages is to log at-bats against the Trajekt machine.
Edgardo Henriquez
Henriquez, the latest Dodgers injury, returned to Los Angeles in order to undergo testing on his back/side area. He was officially put on the 15-day injured list due to low back discomfort, but Roberts noted there might be some trouble with the oblique as well.
Henriquez is not eligible to return during the regular season but the Dodgers hope he will be available for the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages get big injury updates before playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
With a spot in the MLB playoff locked up, the Los Angeles Dodgers have one major goal for the rest of September: get healthy.
Sure, there are sub-storylines to follow, from Josue De Paula filling in at DH, which bullpen arms are getting hot at the right time, and Kyle Tucker figuring it out down the stretch, but for the most part, the Dodgers simply want to take the field in October with their best guys all available for Dave Roberts to call upon.
Fortunately, on Tuesday, Roberts provided fans with some positive updates on that very front, noting that Shohei Ohtani and Andy Pages are trending in the right direction, as reported by The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"Some more from Dave Roberts: Shohei Ohtani hit in the cage today. Hope is still for him to return before the end of the regular season," Ardaya wrote. "Andy Pages hit off the machine today. Plan is for him to do Trajekt next. Bullpen game on Thursday."
After breaking his hand in mid-August in a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates, Pages has missed almost a month as he works back from surgery. And as for Ohtani? Well, after missing four games earlier in the month, he returned for one but didn't ultimately look right, landing on the IL to allow him to recover from a series of injuries that have hampered his production down the stretch.
Without Pages and Ohtani, the Dodgers still found a way to manufacture offense, ripping off their longest win streak of the season, but folding that duo back into the fray, especially with De Paula proving he deserves a spot on the bench as a power-hitting pinch hitter, makes LA all the more dangerous down the stretch.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Freddie Freeman was out of the Dodgers' starting lineup for Monday night's series opener against the Reds at Great American Ball Park as the star first baseman continues to manage soreness in his right knee, which he has described as patellar tendinitis.
It marked the third time in the Dodgers' past five games that Freeman was not in the starting nine. Manager Dave Roberts reaffirmed that he does not believe Freeman will go on the injured list, and he's expected to return to the lineup on Tuesday.
"I just think right now, with where we’re at in the season, an IL is not an option in the sense of -- I personally don’t think we have a better option," Roberts said. "I don’t think it needs to be 10 days. But could it be more than one? That’s a fair question."
Freeman is essentially day to day moving forward. Roberts believes that Freeman's knee has impacted his offensive performance lately, as the 37-year-old is hitting 3-for-30 (.100) with just one extra-base hit in September.
There is some evidence that the knee has been hindering Freeman for longer, as his power numbers have dropped off over the past couple months. He only has one home run in his past 55 games, and he's slugging .350 in that span.
For most of his power drought, Freeman was still hitting for average and consistently getting on base. But when his overall performance took a dip earlier this month, the Dodgers opted to rest him, knowing how important he will be to their offense in the postseason. Freeman is hitting .293 with an .818 OPS in 142 games this season.
Roberts is hopeful that giving Freeman time off now will make it less likely that he'll have to manage his knee throughout the postseason.
"I think that if we can kind of manage it … depending on how the season goes, as far as the recovery," Roberts said. "And then also in the postseason, there’s more off-days. So I think that just trying to get ahold of it, I think that’s the main thing."
The Dodgers' lineup is far from full strength in mid-September, with a dozen regular-season games remaining. Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day IL due to lingering right biceps and left knee issues and won't be eligible to be activated until Sept. 23. Andy Pages is working his way back from a fracture in his left hand and is also unlikely to return until the final week.
Freeman isn't the only active Dodger who is banged up. Miguel Rojas, who exited early on Sunday after aggravating his right shoulder, was back in the starting lineup on Monday. Rojas is sore but playable, so he'll start against the Reds' left-handed starters this week in Cincinnati.
It's commonly said that every player is dealing with some kind of physical issue, big or small, at this point in the season. Not only have the injuries piled up for the Dodgers of late, but they have affected some of their most important hitters.
But for the Dodgers, who entered Monday a win away from clinching their 14th consecutive postseason berth, the rest of the regular season is less consequential than the games that come after. They will use these final two weeks -- and if they finish with a top-two record in the NL, the bye week -- to get their injured players right in time for the postseason.
"Honestly, I think right now it's front of mind, it's not great," Roberts said. "But I will say this: Once you get to October, athletes have a magical way of feeling better. It happens every single year, where there's that extra adrenaline that athletes get when you get to the postseason.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are one win away from clinching a National League playoff berth.
Monday, September 14, the Dodgers begin a three-game series against the Cincinnati Reds for the second time seven games.
Ahead of tonight’s game, the Dodgers make a couple changes in their lineup, one of them involving utility player Tommy Edman.
Tommy Edman is Back in the Lineup vs. the Reds After a Rest Day on Sunday
Per Los Angeles Dodgers reporter David Vassegh, the team announced their starting lineup against the Cincinnati Reds on Monday.
#Dodgers Lineup vs #Reds LHP, Nick Lodolo: Edman CF, Betts SS, Smith C, Tucker RF, T. Hernandez LF, Rojas 2B, Muncy 3B, E. Hernandez 1B, JDP DH, Tarik Skubal SP,” Vassegh wrote on X.
Edman sat out in Sunday’s loss against the Miami Marlins because Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, did not want him playing all three games on a turf field.
“#Dodgers Dave Roberts originally said Josue De Paula would DH all 3 games in Miami,” Dodgers insider Bill Plunket wrote on X ahead of Sunday’s game. “Thought it thru and decided he didn’t want Teoscar Hernandez or Tommy Edman to play all 3 games on turf here. So De Paula gets the start in LF.”
Edman and the Dodgers have been carefully monitoring the center fielder’s ankle, after spending nearly half the season on the injured list. The 31-year-old underwent an offseason ankle surgery and did not return to the Dodgers lineup until June 17.
While the Dodgers primary center fielder Andy Pages, remains on the injured list, Edman has spent most of starts in center.
Despite slashing .257/.339/.390 in 72 games, Edman’s seven game stretch shows signs of a quite the slump.
He’s batting .091 with five strikeouts, two hits, and two RBIs in his last 22 at-bats. Both of hits coming against the Washington Nationals on September 6.
Hopefully yesterday’s much needed rest day gets Edman back where he needs to be.
Los Angeles Dodgers Magic Number to Win NL West is Four
There only 15 days until the first MLB postseason game, and 13 games left in the season for the Dodgers. They can clinch a postseason berth tonight with a win against the Reds.
“LAD can clinch a postseason berth today with a win at Cincinnati *or* losses by both the Padres (@ COL) AND the Diamondbacks (v. MIA),” Dodgers beat writer Katie Woo wrote on X.
For the National League West, the Dodgers’ magic number is four.
After their series concludes against the Reds, the Dodgers are strictly facing NL West opponents. Two series at-home against the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres, and rounding off the season on the road to face San Francisco for the final time in 2026.
